title: Inside NASA's Astronaut Training Hub for the Future!
summary:
Have you ever wondered where astronauts train for their missions? NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas, is the place! And it's changing to get ready for the future of space travel.

Right now, astronauts live on the International Space Station (ISS), but that's going to retire around 2030. So NASA is working with private companies to build new space stations. They're called Commercial LEO Destinations, or CLD for short.

In 2021, NASA gave about $415 million to three companies – Nanoracks, Blue Origin, and Northrop Grumman – to start designing their own space stations. Other companies like Vast Space are also building their own modules.

We got to tour the famous Mission Control, where flight controllers watch over the astronauts on the ISS. Flight director Diane Dailey showed us how they keep an eye on the crew. They even have a live camera view so they can see if the astronauts are busy before calling them.

"We usually have that live camera view just up for awareness. It just helps us understand," she said.

The Mission Control room has lots of screens showing the station's position, communications, and other important data. Controllers sit at their own laptops, each specializing in different systems like propulsion, communications, or computers.

"You're going to see different consoles that specialize in different aspects of spacecraft operations," Dailey explained.

We also learned about the Space Vehicle Mockup Facility, called Building 9. It's like a giant playground for astronauts! They can practice on full-size models of spacecraft and modules. The facility is always changing because different missions need different setups.

NASA is excited to work with private companies to keep humans flying in space. Even when the ISS retires, astronauts will still have places to live and work in orbit. And who knows – maybe one day you'll be an astronaut on a commercial space station!
why_it_matters: Private space stations could shape the future of space jobs and travel, so today's kids might grow up with more chances to live and work in orbit.

keywords.explanation: New space stations that private companies are designing to replace the ISS in low Earth orbit.
A large space station where astronauts from different countries live and work in orbit.
A room where flight controllers watch over astronauts and spacecraft from Earth.
The person in charge of a Mission Control team during a space mission.
A building with full-size models of spacecraft for astronauts to practice in.
Systems that move a spacecraft by pushing it forward.

questions.question: Where is NASA's Johnson Space Center?
What is the International Space Station expected to do around 2030?
In 2021, about how much money did NASA give to three companies to design space stations?
What does Mission Control use to see if astronauts are busy before calling them?
What do different consoles in Mission Control specialize in?

background_read: NASA, the U.S. space agency, has sent astronauts to space for decades and trains them at Johnson Space Center in Texas.
The International Space Station (a large spacecraft where astronauts from many countries live and work) has orbited Earth for many years.
Private companies such as Blue Origin (a space company founded by Jeff Bezos) are now working on new stations with NASA's support.
Article_Structure: WHO: NASA, flight director Diane Dailey, mission controllers, and private companies are preparing for the future of space travel at Johnson Space Center.
WHAT: NASA is working with companies on Commercial LEO Destinations and training astronauts on mockup spacecraft before the ISS retires.
WHERE: This happens in Houston, Texas — mainly in Mission Control and the Space Vehicle Mockup Facility called Building 9.
WHY: NASA wants to keep humans living and working in orbit after the International Space Station retires around 2030.

perspectives.description: NASA and private companies are optimistic that commercial stations will keep astronauts in orbit and create new space jobs.
Some people worry that depending on private companies could change how space exploration is run or make it cost more.
Engineers and planners will compare different station designs to find out which are safest and work best.
